Q: mpi4py conflicts with MS-MPI (msmpi.dll) on Anaconda3 A:

I ran this from the conda base env prompt and the problem is no longer there (which I think is the same effect as removing the files from those 2 directories):

conda remove --force -y msmpi

Q: Reportlab pdf layout guide A: 
FULL PDF GENERATOR CODE
Python
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4

# -------------------------
# STORY PAGES
# -------------------------
pages = [
"Layla Grace David Rennie was five years old.\nShe loved to sing, dance, and dream big dreams.",

"But Layla had a special wish.\nShe wanted to help people and keep everyone safe.",

"When Layla was very little, sad things had happened.\nBut she understood love more than anything.",

"I will be brave. I will help others. I will keep people safe.",

"Layla became a junior coast guard helper by the sea.",

"At night, a soft glowing light filled her room...",

"A silver ladder appeared, leading to a shining rocket in the sky.",

"Inside the rocket were her heroes: Granda Div, Uncle Neil, Uncle Casey, and Nanny Shell.",

"They flew through the stars on a magical mission.",

"One night they found someone struggling in the sea.",

"Layla sang gently to help them stay calm and float safely.",

"The person floated like a starfish. They were safe.",

"You’re safe now, Layla said softly, her heart glowing.",

"We protect people together, her family said.",

"Layla saw a dream world where everyone was safe and happy.",

"She stood strong as a superhero filled with light and courage.",

"I will always help people, she promised.",

"It was time to return home from the stars.",

"Layla snuggled into bed, feeling safe and loved.",

"As she fell asleep she whispered: I’m a superhero."
]

# -------------------------
# CREATE PDF
# -------------------------
def create_pdf(filename="Layla_Starry_Sky_Superhero.pdf"):
    c = canvas.Canvas(filename, pagesize=A4)
    width, height = A4

    for i, text in enumerate(pages):
        c.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 16)
        c.drawCentredString(width/2, height-80, "Layla the Starry Sky Superhero")

        c.setFont("Helvetica", 12)

        lines = text.split("\n")
        y = height - 150

        for line in lines:
            c.drawCentredString(width/2, y, line)
            y -= 25

        c.setFont("Helvetica-Oblique", 10)
        c.drawCentredString(width/2, 40, f"Page {i+1} of {len(pages)}")

        c.showPage()

    c.save()
    print("PDF created successfully!")

# -------------------------
# RUN
# -------------------------
create_pdf()

Q: How can I kill a process running on particular port in Linux? A:

Using this script, which is more user-friendly than other options and checks that the port is actually in use.

Usage: openport 1234

openport() {
  # sed = second line https://stackoverflow.com/a/1429628/152711
  # awk = second word https://unix.stackexchange.com/a/174038
  processId=$(lsof -i tcp:$1 | sed -n 2p | awk '{print $2}')
  if [ ! -z "$processId" ] # Non-null https://www.cyberciti.biz/faq/bash-shell-find-out-if-a-variable-has-null-value-or-not/
  then
    echo Killing $processId
    kill -9 $processId
  else
    echo No process found
  fi
}

Q: Finding the longest two words per input text file - linux A:

So you need to analyze the problem a bit more before laying code. From my understanding of it, you want a report for the tow longest words for each file.

  • You already built a loop for the files passed as arguments to the script. This part is ok, maybe find a more meaningful variable name like file or just f if you like short names.

  • For each file you need a report. So the usual approach is delegate the report processing to a function. Lets call the function:

    reportLongest2names() {}

  • Next what algorithm to get the longest two words? You choose to process the output of strings, it is a nice approach, and will handle binary files as well. Good use of strings, but expanding it this way is not correct for the iteration.

    If you really want to iterate each words in all strings in Shell, you must stream the output and read each value, or here in Bash you can store this output in an array.

    For example:

    # Collects all words from strings in file into an array named words
mapfile -t words < <(strings "$file" | tr '[:space:]' '\n')

# Then it is easy to iterate words
for word in "${words[@]}"; do

    Before iterating, you will need to collect the two longest words. Lets define both variables:

    # Initialize both empty
lgst1=
lgst2=

    Next your current algorithm is mostly correct. Although you were wondering about how to deal with the second longest word. Wen a new longest word is found, the current longest becomes the second longest. It is a down shift.

    Lets now implement the report function with this algorithm:

    #!/usr/bin/env bash

reportLongest2names() {
  # Mandatory file name argument
  file=${1:?}

  # Collects all strings from files into an array named strings
  mapfile -t words < <(strings "$file" | tr '[:space:]' '\n' ) || return 1 # return false if cannot read

  lgst1=
  lgst2=

  # Then it is easy to iterate words
  for word in "${words[@]}"; do
    if [ "${#word}" -gt "${#lgst1}" ]; then
      lgst2=$lgst1
      lgst1=$word
    fi
  done

  # Prints the report for the file
  if [ -n "$lgst1" ]; then
    printf 'In file %s:\n' "$file"
    printf 'Longest word is: %q\n' "$lgst1"
    [ -n "$lgst2" ] && printf '2nd longest word is: %q\n' "$lgst2"
    echo
  fi
}

for arg; do
  reportLongest2names "$arg"
done

Final note:

Bash or the Shell in general is not a good language to process text. Especially loops are very inefficient in shell because commands are executed at each iteration. This algorithm would surely be best handled in awk or if you really want it in shell, at least make use of the core tools like sort, head …
